Mir has chalked a tally by the door: GOOD BANGS and BAD BANGS. Today's goes in a third column, MUSICAL.|You don't even flinch at the bang now. Mir hands you a broom before the smoke clears.} {Gears are still rolling across the floor.|A small cog is spinning on its edge, refusing to fall.|{season == "winter": The blast has blown the window open and snow is coming in.|The fire bucket by the door is already empty.}} Help sweep up and salvage {You sort springs from gears from bits of the ceiling. A spring bites your finger; Mir says that one's always been like that.|You salvage a box of parts and a burnt sleeve. Mir promises to name the next bang after you.|You sweep like a professional now, and pocket a cog that wouldn't fall. Mir pretends not to see. Your fingers are cut in two places.} Read the singed blueprint {You find the mistake, a rune drawn backwards, and tell Mir, who is delighted, then mortified, then delighted. "Probably that's what it was!"|You study the scorched blueprint while Mir sweeps around you, and learn more from the burn marks than from the lines.|You can read Mir's blueprints now, even singed. You show them where today's bang came from. They want to do it again, on purpose.}

results.title: Blueprints
results.excerpt:
Blueprints
Mir has drawn a blueprint for something for you. {~"A lamp that turns itself off when you fall asleep reading," they say. "Probably."|"A pocket that's bigger inside," they say. "In theory. In practice, it eats keys."} They don't say why they keep making things for you.

results.title: Fire in the Workshop
results.excerpt:
Fire in the Workshop
The workshop is on fire. Properly this time. Mir is in the doorway, coughing — and trying to go back in. "My notebooks! Three years of notes!"

results.title: An Explosion in the West Wing
results.excerpt:
An Explosion in the West Wing
The west wing explodes. Not badly. A figure in goggles stumbles out of the purple smoke, coughing, and gives you a thumbs-up. "Don't worry! That was intentional! Mostly! Can you hold this?" They hand you a ticking teapot.
Put the teapot down and back

results.title: It Probably Works
results.excerpt:
It Probably Works
Mir sweeps a bench clear with one arm. "Watch!" A kettle, a mantel clock and a spoon jump together into a whirring thing that pours tea, mostly into the cup. "No plans, no drawings, just ask the bits what they want to be! It's my own. It probably won't explode.
